name: Glaucoma clinics
summary: How expats find glaucoma care in Singapore for high eye pressure, visual-field loss, and family-history screening — including drop adherence in humid climates and when cataract pathways intersect.
body:
Glaucoma quietly steals peripheral vision. Expats often discover raised intraocular pressure on an optical screen or during a parent’s visit to an ophthalmologist. Glaucoma clinics manage diagnosis, drop regimens, laser, and surgery when needed — distinct from routine glasses updates.

## What care involves
- Optic nerve imaging and visual-field testing
- Pressure checks and target-pressure planning
- Daily eye drops (tolerability and adherence matter)
- Selective laser trabeculoplasty and other procedures in selected cases
- Surgical options when fields progress despite medical therapy

Optical shops can flag risk; they do not replace ophthalmology for confirmed or suspected glaucoma.

## Expat practicalities
Shift work and travel across time zones disrupt drop schedules — ask for written timing plans. Generic vs branded drops affect cost; insurance outpatient drug riders vary. Ageing parents on short visits need enough days for fields and follow-up before flying.

## How to choose
Prefer ophthalmologists with glaucoma focus who explain field trends in plain language and do not sell unnecessary premium cataract packages as a glaucoma cure. Bring prior imaging disks and a medication list. If you also have cataracts, ask how combined decisions are sequenced.

## Practical tip
Set phone alarms for drops and keep a travel mini-bottle kit. Missing evening doses for a week before a review falsely suggests “treatment failure.”
whenToEngage: Raised eye pressure or optic-nerve risk on a screen
Family history of glaucoma needs formal assessment
Drop adherence / side-effect plan for travel weeks
Progressive field loss — laser or surgery discussion
